web_title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
book_title: Chapter 2: Inside the Silicon Engine — Nodes, Platforms & Real-World Chips
question: What does TSMC sell across its process nodes, end-market platforms, and packaging lines, and how is each dollar earned?

epigraph.quote: A strong structural demand for our leading-edge process technologies—particularly N3 and the initial ramp of N2—continues to be driven by AI and HPC.
epigraph.author: Wendell Huang, Senior VP & CFO, TSMC (Q3 2026)

web_blocks.text: Revenue Architecture: Technology Nodes, Platforms & Geography
web_blocks.title: Revenue Architecture: Technology Nodes, Platforms & Geography

web_blocks.html: TSMC earns revenue by making custom chips on 300mm (12-inch) and 200mm (8-inch) silicon wafers. It also increasingly assembles multi-chiplet systems via advanced packaging (CoWoS, InFO, SoIC). In FY2025, TSMC posted US$122.42 billion in net sales (NT$3,809.05 billion, +35.9% YoY in USD) and shipped 15.0 million 12-inch equivalent wafers [2, 9]. By Q3 2026, quarterly sales reached US$46.72 billion (NT$1,494.24 billion, +41.2% YoY). Advanced nodes (7nm and below) grew from 74% of wafer sales in FY2025 to 79% in Q3 2026 [5, 9].

web_blocks.caption: TSMC Revenue Mix by Technology Node, Platform & Geography (FY2025–Q3 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: HPC reached 67.9% of Q3 2026 net revenue while leading-edge nodes (<=7nm) climbed to 79% of wafer sales. Customer concentration in U.S.-headquartered accounts rose to 78.9% in Q3 2026 while China fell to 5.5%.

web_blocks.text: Concrete End-to-End Examples by Major Platform
web_blocks.title: Concrete End-to-End Examples by Major Platform

web_blocks.html: 1. High-Performance Computing (HPC — 58% of FY2025 revenue, 66% in Q2 2026) [4, 7]. Take an NVIDIA Blackwell / Rubin AI accelerator or a cloud custom ASIC like Google TPU or AWS Trainium. Who buys & why: NVIDIA (Customer A, 19% of FY2025 sales at ~NT$726.9B / ~$23.2B) [7, 15] needs top transistor density and power efficiency within strict thermal limits. How it is made & billed: TSMC prints the compute dies on custom 4NP (5nm-class) or N3P (3nm-class) EUV lines. Those dies then move to TSMC's CoWoS-L / CoWoS-S packaging line. There, GPU chiplets bond with 8 to 12 High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) stacks on an interposer up to 5.5x+ reticle size [12]. TSMC bills per wafer (often $16,000–$20,000+ per N3 wafer) plus a separate high-margin packaging fee per CoWoS unit. Upfront capacity deals lock in those terms.

2. Smartphone (29% of FY2025 revenue, 22% in Q2 2026) [4, 7]. Take an Apple A18 / A19 mobile SoC or M-series laptop chip (Apple was Customer B at 17% of FY2025 sales, ~NT$645.1B / ~$20.5B) [7, 15]. Qualcomm Snapdragon and MediaTek Dimensity flagship chips also run here. Who buys & why: Phone makers need top performance per watt so flagship handsets run on-device AI without draining batteries. How it is made & billed: Apple acts as TSMC's lead launch partner, anchoring early ramps of N3E/N3P and, in 2026, pioneering N2 (2nm nanosheet GAA) [5, 13]. After wafer fabrication in Taiwan's GigaFabs, mobile SoCs use TSMC's thin InFO-PoP (Integrated Fan-Out Package-on-Package) to stack DRAM atop the logic die. Contracts pair wafer-start fees with volume-tiered yield-sharing terms during early ramps.

3. Automotive (5% of FY2025 revenue) [7]. Take an ADAS autonomous driving controller or zonal microcontroller built for Tier-1 auto suppliers like NXP, Renesas, Infineon, or Tesla/NVIDIA Drive. Who buys & why: Auto silicon demands AEC-Q100 zero-defect quality across extreme temperatures (-40°C to +150°C) and 10–15 year lifecycles. How it is made & billed: High-compute ADAS chips use auto-qualified N5A or N3AE nodes. MCUs and power chips run on mature 16nm/28nm lines, including TSMC's Kumamoto (JASM) fab in Japan and upcoming Dresden (ESMC) fab in Germany [13]. Deals feature multi-year supply guarantees and strict defect-per-billion (DPB) quality premiums.

4. Internet of Things (IoT — 5%) & Digital Consumer Electronics (DCE — 1%) [7]. Take a Wi-Fi 7 / Bluetooth LE RF chip or smartwatch processor from MediaTek, Broadcom, or Nordic Semiconductor. Who buys & why: Edge IoT devices prize ultra-low standby power, mixed-signal analog/RF blocks, and low die cost over raw clock speed. How it is made & billed: TSMC builds these on specialty nodes like N22ULL (Ultra-Low Leakage) or N6RF. They are billed at mature-node wafer rates where depreciated fab gear yields steady cash despite lower ASPs.

Packaging Mix & U.S. Customer Concentration (Q3 2026 Footnote Audit). Note 20a of TSMC's Q3 2026 financial statements splits net revenue into Wafer sales (NT$1,219.77 billion, or 81.6% of Q3 sales) and Others (NT$274.47 billion, or 18.4%, up 112.8% YoY) covering CoWoS, InFO, SoIC packaging, and mask services [21]. Geographically, U.S.-headquartered clients rose from 75% in FY2025 to 78.9% (NT$1,178.52 billion) in Q3 2026, while China fell to 5.5% (NT$81.46 billion) [21]. That shift deepens TSMC's reliance on U.S. hyperscaler and AI accelerator demand.

web_blocks.title: The Two-Toll Booth Model: Front-End Wafer + CoWoS Packaging
paragraphs: Historically, TSMC handed finished wafers to outside OSATs like ASE and Amkor for packaging. In the AI era, CoWoS advanced packaging has become a co-equal profit and moat engine. TSMC now collects both the leading-edge wafer toll and the 2.5D/3D chiplet packaging toll.

book_paragraphs: Ask someone what TSMC sells, and the textbook reply is 'processed silicon wafers.' The real-world answer in 2026 is far stronger. TSMC sells the physical compute substrate of the global economy, and it now collects two separate tolls on every flagship AI system built.

See how fast the mix has shifted in just a few years. For a decade, smartphones anchored TSMC, with Apple alone driving over a fifth of total sales. By FY2025, High-Performance Computing climbed to 58% of TSMC's $122.42 billion revenue. NVIDIA passed Apple as Customer A at 19% of sales versus Apple's 17%. By Q2 2026, HPC surged to 66% of sales while Smartphone eased to 22%. Leading-edge nodes of 7nm and below hit 79% of wafer sales in Q3 2026 as 2nm made its commercial debut.

Let us look inside TSMC's revenue engine to see what drives 2026 results. For nearly ten years, TSMC meant the smartphone cycle, led by Apple's A-series and Qualcomm's Snapdragon chips. That story has changed. By FY2025, High Performance Computing (HPC) reached 58% of sales while phones settled at 29%. In Q3 2026, Note 20a shows HPC hit 67.9% on NT$1,494.24 billion ($46.72 billion) in quarterly sales, while Smartphone held 20.9% and non-wafer packaging and mask revenue jumped 112.8% YoY to 18.4% of total sales.

Just as striking is how fast leading-edge nodes absorb the revenue mix. In Q3 2026, 3nm (N3) alone drove 33% of wafer sales, while 5nm (N5) added 34%–36% across recent quarters. The new 2nm (N2) nanosheet node debuted at 8% of wafer sales, up from 3% just one quarter prior. Together, nodes at 7nm and below now generate nearly four-fifths of wafer sales. Mature nodes (16nm, 28nm, and specialty lines) serve as a steady cash base rather than the growth driver.

book_callouts.title: Why Node Mix Drives Pricing Power
book_callouts.text: Each shift from 5nm to 3nm—and now from 3nm to 2nm nanosheet GAA—lifts wafer prices because transistor density, EUV layers, and complexity rise. Yet clients still pay more per wafer gladly because their cost per billion transistors or per AI FLOP keeps falling.

book_subsections.title: Walking the Cleanroom Floor: Four Real-World Chips
paragraphs: Picture four chips moving through TSMC's fabs right now. First, take an NVIDIA Blackwell or Rubin AI accelerator. NVIDIA's team designs the GPU chiplets and sends layout files to TSMC, which prints them on custom 4NP or 3nm wafers using ASML EUV tools. Instead of shipping bare dies, TSMC routes them into CoWoS packaging lines. There, it bonds logic chiplets and tall HBM stacks onto a large silicon interposer, charging once for the wafer and again for CoWoS integration.

Second, picture an Apple A19 or M-series chip. Apple serves as TSMC's launch anchor on new nodes, funding the early ramp of 3nm and 2nm in return for priority supply and custom tuning. Third, look at an auto ADAS controller or MCU built on N5A or mature 16nm/28nm lines in Taiwan and Japan with zero-defect premiums. Fourth, take a Wi-Fi 7 or wearable RF chip on 22nm ultra-low-leakage silicon—lower wafer prices, yes, but made in paid-off fabs that print high-margin cash.

book_subsections.title: From Wafer Fabrication to System-Level Packaging: Why CoWoS Matters
paragraphs: A modern AI accelerator is no longer one single piece of silicon. Reticle limits cap how big a single GPU die can be printed, so architects split compute dies, I/O dies, and HBM stacks onto a shared interposer. TSMC's Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate (CoWoS) technology wires those chiplets together at micron scale. Across 2025 and 2026, CoWoS—not front-end wafer space—was the main bottleneck for global AI server shipments.

Seeing this shift, TSMC expanded CoWoS capacity from roughly 75,000–80,000 wafers per month in late 2025 toward 120,000–140,000 wafers per month by end-2026. It also outsourced simpler substrate and CoW steps to trusted OSAT partners. For investors, the key point is simple: TSMC captures value twice on every flagship AI chip—once for printing N3 or N2 dies, and again for packaging them with HBM.

book_subsections.title: Geographic Footprint and Customer Concentration in Practice
paragraphs: TSMC's geographic and client mix shows both global reach and rising concentration. Note 20a of the Q3 2026 report shows U.S.-headquartered customers grew from 75% in FY2025 to 78.9% of Q3 2026 revenue (NT$1,178.52 billion), while China declined to 5.5% (NT$81.46 billion) under export curbs. Taiwan accounted for 8.5%, EMEA 3.4%, and Japan 3.0% of quarterly net sales.

At the client level, TSMC's top two buyers—NVIDIA at 19% of FY2025 sales and Apple at 17%—together make up 36% of total revenue. Beneath those two anchors sits a deep roster of compute and network leaders: AMD, Broadcom, Qualcomm, MediaTek, and custom silicon teams at Amazon, Google, and Microsoft. Virtually every major AI training and inference chip relies on TSMC's cleanrooms.

book_subsections.title: Mature Nodes as the Quiet Cash-Flow Anchor
paragraphs: While 3nm and 2nm nodes grab headlines, TSMC's mature and specialty lines quietly anchor cash flow. These span 16nm, 28nm, analog, RF, image sensors, and auto microcontrollers. Because lithography gear in those older fabs is mostly paid off, incremental wafer sales drop straight to operating profit.

Auto and industrial clients also qualify TSMC's specialty processes for seven-to-ten-year product lifecycles. That gives TSMC steady baseline fab utilization even when consumer phone demand swings from quarter to quarter.

book_subsections.title: How Platform Diversity Buffers Single-Cycle Volatility
paragraphs: Even with HPC at 66% of Q3 2026 sales, TSMC's platform mix still matters for fab utilization. Smartphones (26%–29% of sales), IoT, Automotive, and Digital Consumer Electronics span N3, N5, N7, and specialty nodes. That lets TSMC shift wafer starts as seasonal phone builds peak in Q3 while data-center orders ramp all year.
That multi-platform balance keeps Gigafab utilization structurally higher than any single-market chipmaker.
